newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 22.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - New Zealand newspapers - July 22.

text.p: THE DOMINION

Leaders making mischief -- Shipley: High-ranking minister Jenny Shipley accused Prime Minister Jim Bolger and Treasurer Winston Peters on Monday night of "political mischief-making" for suggesting future tax cuts might not go ahead if the compulsory retirement savings scheme lost the September referendum. Page 1.

Speaker asked to rule on Kopu resignation: Alliance leader Jim Anderton has asked Speaker Doug Kidd to get Parliament's privilege committee to rule on whether dissident MP Alamein Kopu in effect resigned from Parliament by leaving the Alliance. Page 1.

Report gets 'forgiving' response from ministers: Senior government ministers are not going to let insulting comments in a secret Australian government report stop them from going to Melbourne to meet counterparts and to enjoy the Bledisloe Cup match. Page 2.
Call for MPs who leave their parties to quit: National junior whip David Carter says MPs who quit their parties should also have to leave Parliament. Page 2.

Navy, air force involved in getting PNG delegates home: Cabinet ministers approved a plan on Monday to divert a navy frigate to act as an escort to make sure Papua New Guinea delegates return home safely from the Bougainville peace talks in Christchurch. Page 2.

World Index Fund draws quick $120m: Superannuation funds and individual investors have pumped more than $120 million into international sharemarkets through AMP Investments' new World Index Fund in just a fortnight. Page 13.
Commission approves Egmont power sale: The Commerce Commission approved the $124.8 million sale of Egmont Electricity to Powerco on Monday. Page 13.
THE NEW ZEALAND HERALD

Luxton sees baby boom as way to fund super: Policies which entice people to go forth and multiply could be the answer to the dwindling ratio of taxpayers to superannuitants, says a government minister.

NGC deal opens gas lines to competition: Natural Gas Corporation's monopoly on the wholesale gas supply business has been broken, heralding increased competition and a possible drop in delivered gas prices.
Myths blamed for clouding dairy debate: Five dangerous myths are being spread on the dairy industry's future structure, says the Dairy Board's chief executive, Warren Larsen.
Minister rules out court bid by Clear: The government will seek to have Clear Communication's bid to enforce undertakings given on telecommunications deregulation thrown out of court.

Bonus boosts chief's pay packet: The managing director of the Pacific Retail Group, Greg Lancaster, received a $203,000 bonus as part of his salary package this year, despite his company's worst performance since it was publicly floated in 1993.

US quarantine row fells lucrative timber exports: Forestry groups are to meet on Thursday to discuss their response to a United States injunction which threatens this country's $100 million-a-year timber exports there.
THE PRESS
Residents rate Chch tops: Survey shows satisfaction: Christchurch people have given their city the thumbs up. Page 1.

NZ eases Aust chagrin: The New Zealand Government has moved to ease Australia's embarrassment over the leaking of a scathing diplomatic report by publicly agreeing that its contents are not Australian Government policy. Page 2.

Income fall with super predicted: More than 1.2 million New Zealanders will have less disposable income under the proposed compulsory superannuation scheme, Transport Minister Jenny Shipley said on Monday night. Page 6.

Goodman says break market still competitive: Having 60 percent of the national packaged bread market was not enough to set market prices, says Goodman Fielder's New Zealand general manager, Colin Wise. Page 27.

Pac Retail plans major spending on stores: Pacific Retail -- the former Noel Leeming chain, now merged with Bond and Bond -- will spend more than $5 million this financial year on opening five new shops and remodelling or resitting another 15. Page 27.
